newsitem.title: SPAIN: Sale of 30 pct of Koipe aimed at institutions.
newsitem.headline: Sale of 30 pct of Koipe aimed at institutions.

text.p: Plans to sell a stake of around 30 percent in Spanish olive oil firm Koipe to institutional investors are in their final stage, sources at the firm told Reuters on Tuesday.
"The share offering will be institutional, and will have a national and international tranche," a spokeswoman said.
The volume of shares offered will represent between 30 and 32 percent of the oil maker's capital.
Medeol, subsidiary of main shareholder Eridania Beghin-Say, will sell around 25 pct, keeping 51 percent.
Corporacion de Alimentacion y Bebidas will sell around four percent, half of its Koipe stake, and Kopinver will sell its 3.01 percent treasury stock.
At market prices, 30 percent of Koipe is worth just under 21.0 billion pesetas. Shares were trading up 0.94 percent to 10,700 pesetas at 1245 GMT.

According to financial daily La Gaceta de los Negocios, there would be some difficulty in setting a price range for the placement given the rise of Koipe shares on the stock market, which have jumped from 7,000 pesetas in late February.
"We are looking at a range of prices for the placement, but there is no hurdle," the spokeswoman said.
Once the design of the placement has been completed, an offer calendar will be issued with a national and international roadshow.
BBV Interactivos and investment bank Schroders are evaluating the placement.
This year trade in Koipe has been dominated by BBV Interactivos, broking around 29 percent of this year's volume so far.
